title: SLO-derived alerting UX compact wireframe
content:
Purpose:

This is a compact UX proposal for surfacing SLO-derived alerts in the Console. Goal is to make alerts actionable and noise-resistant for customers that rely on SLOs (latency, error budget burn) while keeping the configuration surface minimal for common cases.

TL;DR:
- Add an SLO->Alert translation layer in the Alerts UI: customers pick an SLO and choose a behavior (notify, throttle, auto-snooze).
- Default heuristics for thresholds: burn rate windows, absolute vs relative thresholds, alert suppression during rollouts.
- Compact alert card and drill-in flow so on-call sees signal + quick remediation links (recent traces, model variant, recent deploys).
- Backlog items outlined with rough story points and dependencies.

Context / problem statement:
Teams struggle with two things in current Console: (1) mapping observed SLO regressions into meaningful alerts without creating noise, (2) understanding whether an alert is transient (deploy spike) or systemic (regression). Current alert creation is too low-level for SLO-first workflows; customers re-create the same burn-rate logic in external tooling.

User personas:
- Platform SRE (primarily configures team-wide SLOs and default alerting)
- App owner / ML engineer (wants minimal ops noise and quick links to model telemetry)
- On-call (needs concise context + one-click escalation or mute)

User stories (high level):
- As an SRE, I want to create an alert tied to an SLO that uses recommended defaults so I don’t hand-tune burn rate windows for each service.
- As an ML engineer, I want alerts to include the last 3 model rollouts and top failing prompts so I can triage quickly.
- As an on-call, I want to snooze alerts for a fixed window from the alert card and optionally attach a postmortem link when resolving.

Wireframe notes (compact view + drill-in):
1) Alerts list: grouped by SLO if applicable, compact card shows: SLO name, current burn-rate/remaining budget, trend sparkline (30m-24h), primary channel icon (email/Slack/pager), severity tag, and a short reason (eg. "burn rate >5x (10m)").
2) Quick actions on card: acknowledge, snooze (15m/1h/4h), escalate (opens channel chooser), view traces, assign to owner.
3) Drill-in header: full SLO summary (SLO target + window), recent deploys (last 3), model variant history (if ML model is a target), current error budget line chart with annotated events (deploys, config changes).
4) Signal attribution panel: top correlated dimensions (region, model-variant, request-path), recent sample requests (scrubbed), and a link to "Open evaluation set" for quality checks.
5) Config accordion: indicates the heuristic used to convert SLO->alert (burn-rate window, optional absolute threshold override, suppression rules during canary). The accordion is collapsed by default and includes a "preview" showing how many alerts this config would have generated in last 7 days (sampled).

Heuristics proposal (default behavior):
- Recommended default: 10m burn-rate window with a 5x burn threshold for P1, 3x for P2, and relative thresholds for non-critical SLOs.
- Absolute overrides: customers can set an absolute error-rate floor (e.g., if error rate < 0.1% then ignore burn spikes).
- Suppression rules: suppress alerts for SLOs tagged with "in-rollout" for the first 30m after a deploy unless burn rate exceeds 10x. Explicit canary tag allows immediate exceptions.
- Dedup window: group alerts from same SLO by 10m buckets to avoid repeated notifications during a transient spike.

Telemetry & prefilling: how we make it low-friction
- When user selects an SLO, prefill severity based on SLO target (e.g., 99.9% -> P1), and suggest channels from org-level defaults.
- Show admission control: a small inline simulator that shows expected alert volume (low/medium/high) based on last 7 days.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- SLO->Alert creation flow exists in Console with default heuristics and ability to override.
- Compact alert cards show required fields and quick actions.
- Drill-in includes deploys and model variant history for the last 72h.
- Basic suppression during deploys works and prevents at least 80% of deploy-related noise in lab replay.

Backlog grooming (rough):
- RED-201: SLO->Alert translation backend + API (8 pts) 
- RED-202: Compact alert card UI + quick actions (5 pts)
- RED-203: Drill-in telemetry panels (deploys, model-variant timeline) (8 pts)
- RED-204: Alert-simulation preview (3 pts)
- RED-205: Suppression rules + canary integration (5 pts)
- RED-206: On-call snooze/ack API + audit log (3 pts)
- RED-207: Add "Open evaluation set" link + sample requests (2 pts)
Dependencies: event bus for deploy annotations (infra), model-variant metadata from model registry (applied-ml team), SLO store updates (monitoring infra).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should default suppression be? Too aggressive hides real incidents; too conservative leaves noise. Suggest starting conservative (suppress deploy-window) and expose a visible override.
- Should we support synthetic "composite" SLOs (across multiple endpoints) in the first iteration? Probably not for MVP. Note: high customer demand from platform teams for composite SLOs but adds complexity to attribution.
- Notification cost: preview needs to give a long-run estimate of notifications per week; where should that be surfaced in billing UX? (product + finance).

Sketches / layout notes to hand off to design:
- Compact card: 320px wide, two-line title, right-aligned sparkline, small pill severity. Hover shows expanded quick-actions.
- Drill-in: 3-column layout: (1) SLO summary + actions, (2) charts (budget + trend), (3) attribution (dimensions + sample requests). Mobile collapse priority: show SLO summary and one chart.

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: customers will misconfigure suppression and miss regressions. Mitigation: default conservative suppression, clear inline warnings and a visible history of suppressed alerts with reason.
- Risk: expensive preview simulation. Mitigation: sample-based preview (not full re-compute).

Next steps / owner ask:
- UX: quick low-fi mockups for compact card and drill-in (Jonah) — due EOD next Thu.
- Infra: confirm deploy annotation availability and latency (Luis) — sync on Mon.
- Applied-ML: confirm model variant metadata APIs and permission model (Priya) — blocked until registry PR.

Notes to self:
- Keep the config accordion shallow; aim for "safe defaults" and a single advanced page for power users.
- Capture a couple of replayed incidents to test suppression heuristics.

References and examples:
- Linked internal playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRD/SLO+Alerting+Overview
- Example customer request thread in Slack: slack://thread/GPZ9AB2/topical-slo-thread
